title: Cyber, State Actors and Critical Third Parties
summary: Why state-sponsored cyber activity and dependence on a small number of critical providers create severe but plausible scenarios, and what boards should require on resilience.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why state-sponsored cyber activity and dependence on a small number of critical providers create severe but plausible scenarios, and what boards should require on resilience.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the threat from state actors and organised cyber groups
Assess concentration and dependency on critical third parties
Evaluate the firm's ability to withstand and recover from severe disruption
Syllabus: State-sponsored attacks, disruption and supply-chain compromise
Cloud, data and infrastructure concentration risk
Severe but plausible scenarios and impact tolerances
Board questions on testing, exit plans and recovery
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors, especially members of risk and strategy committees
Executive directors, chief risk officers and senior managers responsible for strategy and emerging risk
Company secretaries, heads of governance and strategy teams supporting the board
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist knowledge of geopolitics, technology or climate science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
TNFD, Recommendations of the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (2023)
